subject: Storage adapter commercial criteria — feedback on deck
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@pinecone.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Rossi <m.rossi@weaviate.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + commercial criteria for storage adapter deck

Hi Kimberly and Vanessa,

Thanks again for the time last week. As promised I've attached a short criteria doc that Palo Alto and a couple of our mutual customers asked us to check against when evaluating a storage adapter (latency tail, object lifecycle, encryption at rest, snapshot compatibility).

High level asks from Pinecone side:
- Clear ownership split for support and escalations (pinecone vs redwood).
- SLA targets for cold-tier retrieval (99th percentile under 1s for indexed queries).
- Retention/expiry semantics exposed to the customer (S3 lifecycle mapping).
- Commercial model: per-index footprint + egress band vs per-query.

I'm copying Marco from Weaviate — we wanted to make sure the criteria are broadly compatible across vendors so customers don't have to rework prompts or pipelines when toggling vector stores.

Attached: redwood_storage_adapter_criteria_v1.pdf (notes inline).

Next steps: could you review and tell us which items are blockers for Redwood commercial approval? We can then produce a one-page term sheet draft.

Best,
Elena
Senior BD, Pinecone

Attachments: redwood_storage_adapter_criteria_v1.pdf
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@pinecone.io>, Marco Rossi <m.rossi@weaviate.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + commercial criteria for storage adapter deck

Thanks Elena — great summary and useful framing. Sequence from our side: product vet -> infra/ops risk review -> commercial terming.

Quick notes after an initial skim:
- SLA expectations: we can't promise 99th <1s for cold-tier across every customer/storage region. We can commit a cold-tier SLO for standardized configs (see page 4) and offer a fast-path (cached-prefetch) option as an add-on.
- Support split: agree we should codify an escalation matrix. Marcus, can you propose a minimal 3-level matrix (Partner support / Redwood L2 / Redwood L3) and expected RTOs?
- Retention mapping: product would like explicit mapping between embedding TTL and S3 lifecycle rules (e.g., 30/90/365 day tiers). Dev, can you confirm if our current persistence layer exposes TTL hooks to S3 lifecycle?
- Commercial: asking for both per-index footprint and egress makes sense. Procurement will push back on per-query.

I'll take the criteria doc and produce a 1-pager term sheet draft for the commercial team. I'll attach the draft and flag the items we've marked as negotiable vs non-negotiable.

Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_coop_term_sheet.docx

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 10:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + commercial criteria for storage adapter deck

Kimberly — draft approach below (short). I'm copying priorities so we can drop into the term sheet.

Escalation matrix (proposed):
1) Partner-facing support (48hr ack for high-sev, 24hr for critical) — partner owns first-level triage.
2) Redwood L2 (SLA-driven, 8hr RTO for critical incidents).
3) Redwood L3 (engineering, 24hr RTO for fixes, hotpatch path for P1).

SLA carve-outs: cold-tier retrieval SLO will exclude customer misconfiguration, cross-region failovers, and vendor storage outages. We can run a joint runbook and a quarterly tabletop for major customers.

Dev note (Dev Patel): TTL hooks — yes, our persistence layer emits lifecycle metadata to the object store; will add a short API contract for mapping TTL -> S3 lifecycle ID. I'll drop a short spec in the shared doc.

Also recommend we standardize a benchmark harness (small set of queries + 99th/95th percentile capture) that partner vendors run to certify adapter releases. That will reduce back-and-forth in sales cycles.

Marcus
Director, Product Ops

Perfect — thanks for the rapid turnaround team. We reviewed Marcus' escalation matrix internally and that tracks. Two quick asks before we share the term sheet with a pilot customer (Acme Retail):

1) Can Redwood confirm whether the benchmark harness will be public (partners can run locally) or require a joint run? Public is preferred for speed.
2) Procurement asked for a signal that there will be a co-marketing commitment (one joint case study + two webinar slots within 12 months). Can you confirm?

I've attached a filled-in term sheet with small edits and a DocuSign link for Pinecone's signature once redwood confirms the two asks.

Elena
